excerpt: Ardent creates instant, isolated copies of your production Postgres database — in seconds, right from your terminal.
Test migrations, run schema changes, and let coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor actually verify their database work — all against real data, without touching production.
Any Postgres — Supabase, RDS, PlanetScale, or self-hosted.
No more shared staging databases. No more hand-maintained fixtures. An instant database for every task.
With the ardent-cli skill installed, a short ask is enough — the skill fetches the current docs and works through setup
Preflight checks whether Ardent can branch this database. It creates nothing and stores no credentials — it just tells you what, if anything, to fix.
If it's interrupted, resume with: ardent connector retry-setup <name>

ardent branch create pr-123 --print-url    # prints only the connection URL
ardent branch info my-feature --format json # prints a stable JSON object
The CLI remembers three things: your current project, connector, and branch. Commands act on the current one unless you say otherwise.
Set ARDENT_TOKEN and run commands normally — no login step
Errors are JSON too, with a stable `code`
--url-type <type> | Which URL to print: direct (default), pooled, or prisma
For the same connector, branch name, and service type, a re-run picks up the original request instead of starting a second one.
Use the API when you are building CI systems, internal developer platforms, custom dashboards, or agent workflows.
role_org_viewer | Read-only automation and reporting
Lock deletion | POST /v1/connectors/{connector_id}/deletion-lock | Blocks deletes until unlocked
Release quarantine | POST /v1/connectors/{connector_id}/quarantine/{quarantine_id}/release | Resumes a paused deployment
Your script or CI harness runs the CLI; the agent only ever sees a branch URL. The agent needs no Ardent token and can't touch anything but its branch.
The agent runs the Ardent CLI itself — creating, using, and deleting its own branches
Every PR runs against its own fresh database branch cloned from your connected source — no shared staging that drifts, no test runs corrupting each other
Ardent lets you run your full test suite, including destructive operations, against an exact copy of production.
Index validation: try a new index and see if it actually speeds up your real queries
Only metadata (schema structure, replication status, branch state) flows from the data plane to the control plane. Your actual data never leaves the data plane.
If a branch URL is ever compromised, it has zero access to your original database. This makes it safe to hand branch URLs to AI agents
you can run SQL on every new branch from this connector after it is created.
Let agents clean, deduplicate and standardize data on an exact copy of production
Clones load in 6s, scale to 0, autoscale compute and do not duplicate storage. Zero management needed
Unlimited branches per database
$30 one-time credit ... Base plan + compute and storage. Never pay for idle resources.

Skeptic of the claim that Ardent 'never impacts production data': testing on real data can cause side effects outside the DB. If you store OAuth tokens for customer integrations, a bad API call can mess up customer data ('been there done that'). Says a read replica covers careful prod testing, so they don't see the need for a SaaS.
Commenter questioned the premise of giving an LLM agent full read access to production data: 'That seems nuts to me.'
Comparison: asked what Ardent's moat is and how it differs from the database branching Neon and Supabase already offer.
Noted Ardent doesn't look open-source. Recommended Xata (ZFS-based, like Delphix) as an open-source alternative for Neon-style or git-like Postgres branching.

On Postgres 18 with xfs and file_copy_method=CLONE, you can clone a database instantly with CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE ... STRATEGY=FILE_COPY. Still thinks Ardent can be useful because cloud providers run heavily restricted Postgres, e.g., Aurora doesn't even allow configuring log_line_prefix.

Says DB clones have been a game changer for their team, giving agents isolated workspaces for query/view optimization and UI work against real data combinations. They self-host DBLab because they had trouble configuring Xata, Neon, and hosted DBLab.
Pointed out Ardent is built on Neon Twin infrastructure and questioned the added value, saying the same can be done using Neon directly for half the cost.

From building browser automation agents that test DB migrations: the real pain wasn't getting a sandbox quickly but that reverting changes after a failed test took forever with traditional backup/restore. Asked whether Ardent offers a synthetic data layer for agents that shouldn't touch real user data.
Pricing complaint: paying $250/month for $100/month in credit 'would kind of bum me out... feels like I'm losing $150/month.'
Asked how cloning handles large data, citing their own 35GB table.

Thinks Ardent makes sense for teams where several agents/developers each need their own environment before deploying. For a solo founder, the real constraint is self-discipline and not skipping review: migrations can be correct yet break live services or lock tables.
